title: Every pane says what it is for, in words somebody already knows
goal: The panel's sections are named in words the app invented, so you have to open one to find out what it does and open it again next time because the name never told you. Somebody looking at a component sees Versions and Adjustable and can tell you what neither of them is for. Name every section for the job it does, using the words this kind of tool already uses, so the panel becomes predictable.
notes:
Said by the user on 2026-09-15 while looking at a component: "i don't even know what 'Versions' is", then "what the hell is adjustable? Component properties? How is 'adjustable' different from anything? This is completely messy IA and ux", and then the summary that should govern this task: "panes purposes should be predictable and clear. It is neither now."

TWO INVENTED NAMES WHERE STANDARD ONES EXIST, and the user guessed the right answer for one of them out loud.

1. 'Adjustable' is this app's word for the things a copy can be given its own values for. Every other tool calls those properties or parameters. The user's own guess, 'Component properties?', is almost certainly the answer, and the fact that they had to guess is the bug. The word also fails on its own terms: everything in the panel is adjustable, so it does not distinguish anything, which is exactly what they said.

2. 'Versions' is this app's word for what the rest of the industry calls variants. This is already recorded as a known divergence: the tutorial guide componentVersions carries a comment saying 'It is called Versions because that is what the panel calls it. The task that asked for this track said Variants, and a guide teaches what shipped rather than what the plan called it.' So the plan said variants, the panel said versions, and the tutorial had to follow the panel. Fix the panel and the rest lines up.

The deeper rule the user is asking for is predictability, so do not stop at two renames. Go through every section and ask whether its name answers 'what is this for'. Where a section needs a paragraph inside it to explain itself - and several do, Versions has three lines of prose under it in the screenshot - the paragraph is a symptom and the name is the disease.

This is the same complaint as the clutter tasks filed alongside it and should be read with them: position-and-size-leave-the-panel, one-row-for-a-number-that-has-four-sides, the-panel-shows-the-panes-that-matter-and-you-ca, and a-copy-of-a-component-is-configured-not-authored. A shorter panel full of unclear names is still unpredictable, and clear names on a wall of sections are still a wall.

Renaming is cheap to do and expensive to do halfway. The tutorials point at panel sections by name and there is a check that fails the build when a guide points at something that has gone, so a rename that misses a guide will be caught - but only if the guides are rebuilt, so run them.

THE MODEL, corrected by the user on 2026-09-15 while walking away. First: "I don't think 'Variants' is any better. component properties makes sense. Variant is a property of the component." Then, still thinking: "Maybe State is a separate property. or maybe variant is hierarchical."

So the direction is ONE concept, not two sections. A component has PROPERTIES. What the panel currently splits into 'Adjustable' and 'Versions' is one list: a property is anything a copy can be given its own answer for, and one KIND of property is a set of named looks, which is what Versions is today. That is why neither name worked: they are two names for halves of one idea.

This also collapses the copy's panel into the same list with values in it instead of definitions, which is what the sibling task a-copy-of-a-component-is-configured-not-authored is for.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, and the user was explicitly unsure, so settle it with a prototype rather than a preference:
- Is a state just one property among many, named State with the values rest, hovered, pressed and disabled? That is the simplest answer and probably right.
- Or does a component need more than one look-changing property at once, so that a Button has a Type of primary or secondary AND a State of rest or hovered, and the two combine into a matrix of drawings? That is what the user means by variant being hierarchical, and it is what real button components need almost immediately.
The second is strictly more powerful and strictly more work, and the first is a special case of it. Prototype the matrix case before choosing, because designing for one look-changing property and discovering later that two are needed is a rewrite rather than an addition.

Do NOT settle this by picking a word. The question is whether the model holds one named-set property or several, and the naming falls out of the answer.
acceptance: Every section in the panel is named for what it is for, and the audit lists each name with the one sentence that justifies it
Versions and Adjustable in particular are renamed to what they actually are, using terms somebody who has used a design tool would recognise rather than terms this app coined
A section's name plus one short line is enough to know whether to open it, without opening it

The explanatory paragraphs currently sitting inside sections are cut back hard: a section that needs three lines of prose to explain itself is misnamed, and the audit says which ones were fixed by renaming rather than by rewording
The same names are used everywhere they appear: the panel, the menus, the tutorials and the tooltips do not use three words for one thing
Nothing is renamed without following it through: grep for the old word and fix the guides, walks and help text that used it, or the app teaches a word it no longer uses
A first-time check with somebody who has not seen it: they can say what each section is for from the name alone, and whatever they got wrong is written down
Audit under queue/audits/ with the panel before and after for a component original, a component copy and a plain shape, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: user corrected the direction: one Properties list, with a variant or state as a kind of property; open question whether several look-changing properties combine

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW before building. Walked the original's Component section as a first-time user from the real capture (component-versions-1-original-sc.png): Name, 'This is the original', a switch with a two-line paragraph, a Versions header with a THREE-line paragraph and an Add, then an Adjustable header with an Add. Two Adds, two headers, two invented words, and the two paragraphs exist only because the headers do not say what they are for. Findings: (1) 'Versions' collides with document version history, which is the other thing that word means in an editor, so it is not merely vague, it is wrong; (2) 'Adjustable' is an adjective where every other header is a noun for a thing, so it does not even read as a list; (3) the copy's panel already IS a properties list (Version row, Label row) with no header, so the original is the only side that is split in two. Shortest version that delivers the same value: ONE list called Properties on both sides, with the look-set as a row in it rather than a section above it. Cut: nothing else on the section is decorative. Kept but shortened: the Share paragraph.

MODEL SETTLED (the open question in the task notes). Prototyped the matrix on paper against the existing store and the answer is: SEVERAL look-changing properties, but a SPARSE set of drawings rather than a full product. A version today is a whole main layer on the canvas, so Type(2) x State(4) as a full matrix means eight drawings hand-edited, and a third property means twenty-four, which is unusable. Addressing a drawing by a tuple of option answers instead of one name is additive over the existing store (each drawing keeps its versionID; it gains an answer per look-property), and a combination nobody drew falls back to the nearest one, so you draw the looks you need instead of filling a grid. That makes one look-property the n=1 case, exactly as the user guessed, WITHOUT painting us into it. The naming falls out: a component has PROPERTIES; a variant is one of them; its options are the looks. So the panel must render a LIST of variant rows, not a Versions section, even while the list holds one.

BUILT. Core: ComponentVariantProperty.swift (componentVariantProperties returns a LIST, componentVariantName, renameComponentVariantProperty) + a variantName field on GroupContent that only writes when renamed, with 11 tests. Default option names are now Default / Variant 2 / Variant 3; the shelf tile counts variants; Apply to Other Variants; Variant added / Variant deleted. Panel: ComponentVersionList is gone, ComponentPropertyList is headed Properties and holds the variant rows first then the knob rows, with ONE Add whose first section is Variant (A second look / Another look). A copy's section grew the same Properties heading and its top row wears the variant property's own name. Menus: Layer > Add Variant. Every user-facing 'knob' is now 'property'; Make X Adjustable is Make X a Property. Tutorials and 18 walks follow. Scripts/test.sh green (6922 tests).

EVERY SECTION NAME, with the sentence that justifies it (acceptance 1). The dock's own section titles were all already nouns a design-tool user knows and none were renamed: Layers (the stack of things in the picture), Component (what this thing is as a reusable piece), Position & Size (where it is and how big), Appearance (how it is painted), Effects (what is added on top), Layout (how a container arranges what is inside it), Arrange (aligning and distributing several things), Frame (a screen's own settings), Columns (the grid a screen is designed to), Text (type settings), Color (paint), Annotation (a redline mark's settings), Measure and Measurements (one measurement, and the list of them), Zoom Callout and Lens (two named features, each its own noun), Collage (a named feature), Canvas (the page itself), Motion (movement over time), Shadow (the shadow), Library (the shelf). The disease was entirely INSIDE Component, which is where the user found it: Versions and Adjustable, now one list called Properties with a Variant row in it.

PARAGRAPHS, fixed by renaming or by rewording (acceptance 4). Fixed by RENAMING: the three-line paragraph under Versions ('One drawing. Adding a version copies it, so this component can hold a second look, like Disabled, under the same name.') is gone outright, because a row called Variant with its looks listed under it does not need explaining; the Adjustable empty state ('Anything you add here is a knob every copy can set on its own') is one shorter line under a heading that now carries the meaning. Fixed by REWORDING, and said so: the Share across documents note was two or three lines and is now one short line ('In this document only.'), because that name was never the problem. Left alone: the 'This is the original. N copies follow it.' line, which is a fact about this component rather than an explanation of a word.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW of the built thing, done by reading rather than using, because the screen was locked. Two things I could not fix and would not guess at: (1) the variant row now carries a name field and each look under it carries another, so there are two name fields stacked, and whether they read as different things is a question for the user - it is in the audit's evaluate list; (2) making a second look costs one more click than it did (open Add, pick A second look) because there is one Add instead of two, which is the price of one predictable list and is also in evaluate. One thing I did fix on re-reading: a copy showing several looks but with no other properties would have printed the Properties heading, a variant row, and then a line saying the original has no properties yet, which contradicts itself; the line now only appears when there is neither.

LEFT ROUGH, under the follow-up bar. Adding a stored property to GroupContent left a stale PhotonzRender in .build and two GroupClipRenderingTests failed on wrong pixels for about twenty minutes until 'swift package clean' fixed it. Real trap for the next runner who touches a Core struct, but it is a build-cache artifact rather than a defect in the app and nobody using Photonz can hit it, so it goes here rather than into a task. Also left rough: the walk step ids and output file names still say version (2-version-added, version-row-name-walk), which only an agent reads; renaming them would churn every baseline path for no reader's benefit.

The Component section is one list called Properties. Versions and Adjustable are gone: a variant is now a ROW in that list, with a name the author can change to State or Type and its looks under it, and the copy's panel reads the same list under the same heading with that same name on its top row. Add Variant and Apply to Other Variants replace the old menu rows, every user-facing 'knob' is now 'property', and the tutorials, help text and 18 walks follow. The model holds a LIST of variant properties, not one, so a Type AND a State is an addition rather than a rewrite; that question is settled and written up in docs/design/ui-building.md. Verified by Scripts/test.sh (6922 tests green, including 11 new ones for the variant property) and swift build. NOT verified by eye: the Mac's screen locked at about 08:53 and stayed locked, so no walk could run and the audit has the before pictures only. Sweep requested.
